Figure 1: GEM mechanism (schematic at a fixed state in a 2-D action space). Training (top row): GEM learns three ingredients that will be combined only at test time: (i) a multimodal actor πθ(a | s) (left; shown as log πθ(a | s)) that preserves multiple plausible action hypotheses, (ii) an independent behavior density µφ(a | s) (middle; shown as logµφ(a | s)) used to quantify dataset support, and (iii) a conservative value statistic LCBλ(s, a) from a critic ensemble (right). Inference (bottom row): given a queried state s, GEM samples N candidates in parallel and adds a deterministic anchor (triangle), scores each candidate using Eq. 4 (conservative value plus behavior-normalized support), and executes the top-ranked action a⋆ (star). The green cluster highlights the small subset of candidates that remain competitive after scoring, illustrating how the interface filters many proposals down to a support-aligned, high-value choice under maximization.
